claims.text: The starting catalyst is a high-entropy alloy containing multiple principal elements in nearly equiatomic ratios.
The starting HEA catalyst loses activity and has durability limitations under transient and low-temperature operation.
A low-Pt synthesis method can disperse single Pt atoms within HEA nanoparticles.
The intervention produces isolated Pt sites embedded in the HEA nanoparticle lattice.
Isolated Pt atoms create highly active catalytic centers.
The isolated Pt centers lower the activation energy of exhaust-gas reactions.
Lowering the activation energy enhances low-temperature catalytic performance.
The high-entropy matrix stabilizes isolated Pt sites against sintering and deactivation.
Stabilization of the Pt sites extends catalyst durability.
Relative to the untreated HEA catalyst, the Pt-treated catalyst will have higher low-temperature catalytic activity.
Relative to the untreated HEA catalyst, the Pt-treated catalyst will better retain performance after thermal aging.
Relative to the untreated HEA catalyst, the Pt-treated catalyst will have improved resistance to poisoning effects.
The activity and durability improvements can be achieved while maintaining low Pt consumption.
The predicted benefits are expected under transient low-temperature exhaust cycling with H2O and NO and after thermal-aging or mileage-mimicking treatment.
The findings may not extend to operating conditions more extreme than the specified vehicular-exhaust conditions.
The magnitude of improvement and the long-term stability of isolated Pt under continuous cycling and mechanical stress remain uncertain.
